# RETRO: t3-12485-881cd11e

## What worked

- A single neutral brief naming the Starship and Neovim sources as in scope let both reviewers resolve the material questions (config path resolution, missing-file fallback, symlink write-through) from upstream source.
- Cross-examination changed the outcome: Sol's final did not contain the edit-loss issue and Opus's did not treat headless activation as a defect. Targeted neutral follow-ups gave independent confirmation of edit loss and settled that the accent gap is pre-existing across 14 templates, which kept a non-PR-specific issue out of the public comment.
- Opus's negative and mutation controls on the staging test separated real coverage from a pass that proves nothing.

## Process deviations (recorded, evidence retained)

- Opus reviewer: first call printed the whole brief with `cat` (about 60 lines) and ran `ls -la` (owner-name resolution) before reading the first-call rules; one parallel pair of reads (90 lines aggregate) and about three single reads exceeded the 60-line bound; one host `python3 -c` parse of downloaded Arch package JSON. None touched the reviewed code or host config. Public claims rest on sealed review.py runs and source, so the deviations do not affect technical conclusions.
- Sol reviewer: one external-source read requested 100 lines (brief bound 50).
- Coordinator: read this team's previous brief (t3-12502, a different PR) as a format template. It contains no technical conclusions relevant to this PR. Worktree creation from the blob:none clone lazily fetched blobs into the assignment's own object store at pin time (before reviewers started); reviewers used `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`.
- Sol job printed "No project session found ... creating a new session" at start; expected for a fresh session.

## Improvements

- The brief's first-call rules do not stop a reviewer from `cat`-ing the whole brief as its first call, because the rules are inside the brief. The Opus dispatch prompt is fixed by policy to one sentence; consider adding the 50-line and `ls -1` rules to the omarchy-reviewer agent definition itself.
- Sol finished in 7.6 minutes with a source-only review and missed the documented-edit path; the cross-check follow-up is worth keeping as standard.

## Tool notes

- `pi_job.py`, `review_team.py subagents`, `check-comment`/`check-result` all worked without intervention. No Markdown renderer on host; a small assignment-local renderer (`tools/render_html.py`) produced the HTML.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the themed Starship config renders correctly and the installed-theme denial works. Two issues were found in how the new hook takes over `~/.config/starship.toml`.

- The template renders for all 22 stock themes with no leftover placeholders. Starship 1.26.0 (the current Arch package) loads it without warnings, and with colour stripped the prompt text is identical to the current `config/starship.toml`. Only five styles change, from ANSI cyan to the theme's accent, red and blue.
- Denying `starship.toml` to git-installed themes is necessary: Starship runs `[custom]` module commands through a shell. The updated `theme-staging-test.sh` fails on the base code and when `starship.toml` is removed from `INSTALLED_THEME_DENIED`, and passes on the PR head and on the current `quattro` tip with the PR applied.
- The hook links a missing target or an untouched default copy, leaves a customised regular file or a directory alone, is idempotent and honours `STARSHIP_CONFIG`.

### Edits to `~/.config/starship.toml` are lost at the next theme switch

After the hook runs, `~/.config/starship.toml` is a symlink into `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/`. `omarchy-theme-set` deletes and rebuilds that directory on every theme set (`rm -rf "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH"` followed by `mv`). `manual/40-prompt.md` and the Omarchy agent skill tell users to customise the prompt by editing `~/.config/starship.toml`. Neovim, the default editor, keeps symlinks when saving (`backupcopy=auto`), and shell redirection also writes through the link. The edit therefore lands in the generated file:

```text
hook runs      ~/.config/starship.toml -> ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/starship.toml
user edits     nvim ~/.config/starship.toml   (writes through the link; prompt changes)
theme switch   rm -rf current/theme; mv next-theme current/theme
result         link now points at a freshly generated file; the edit is gone, no backup or notice
```

Reproduced in an isolated home with a shell append and with `nvim --clean`.

**Impact:** every default install converted by the hook (an absent file or an unmodified default copy) is affected. A customisation made the documented way works at first and then disappears silently.

**Suggested change:** write a regular copy instead of a link, record its hash under `~/.local/state/omarchy`, and replace the target only when it still matches the last generated copy or the shipped default. Edited copies then fall under the existing `cmp` rule and are preserved. If the link is kept, update `manual/40-prompt.md` and the skill to point customisation at `~/.config/omarchy/themed/starship.toml.tpl` (a user template, which keeps theme colours and was confirmed to take precedence) or at replacing the link with a regular file.

### Any existing symlink at the target is replaced

`[[ -L $STARSHIP_TARGET ]]` in `bin/omarchy-theme-set-starship` treats every symlink as Omarchy's own.

| Target before the theme switch | Result |
|---|---|
| absent, or regular copy identical to the shipped default | linked to the generated file |
| regular file with user changes | left untouched |
| symlink to `~/dotfiles/starship.toml` (Stow, dotbot, Home Manager style) | **replaced** by the Omarchy link |
| `STARSHIP_CONFIG` path that is a user symlink | **replaced** by the Omarchy link |

**Impact:** users who manage their Starship config through a dotfiles symlink lose their prompt on every theme switch. The dotfiles file itself is not modified, but restoring the link only lasts until the next switch. On a pre-quattro upgrade, migration `1787481315` runs `omarchy-theme-refresh`, so the replacement also happens during the upgrade.

**Suggested change:** replace a symlink only when `readlink` matches `$STARSHIP_SOURCE` (or points into `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/`), and leave other symlinks alone.

### Smaller notes

**Activation on install and update:** `install/user/theme.sh` runs `omarchy-theme-set` headless, which skips `post_theme_commands`, and the PR adds no install step or migration. Fresh installs and existing quattro users keep the current prompt until their first interactive theme switch or theme refresh. btop, Pi, Hermes and the browser hook each have an explicit install or upgrade step. Adding one here would also spread the edit-loss issue above to every default user, so that issue is worth settling first.

**Dangling link:** switching to a theme with neither `colors.toml` nor `alacritty.toml` generates no `starship.toml`, so the hook exits early and leaves the link dangling. Starship then silently falls back to its stock two-line prompt. Falling back to `$OMARCHY_PATH/config/starship.toml` in that case would keep the Omarchy prompt.

**Documentation:** the ignored-file notice in `bin/omarchy-theme-set` names `starship.toml` but explains that a git-installed theme "cannot supply Lua, a terminal config, or vscode.json". The rationale comment above `INSTALLED_THEME_DENIED`, `docs/theming.md` ("What an installed theme may not ship") and `default/agents/skills/omarchy/theming.md` also omit `starship.toml`. A short reason fits: Starship `[custom]` modules run shell commands.

**Test scope:** source review of the PR head against its merge-base and the current `quattro` tip, plus Starship 1.26.0 and Neovim option sources. Isolated command-only runs with synthetic home directories executed the real template rendering and `starship prompt` for all stock themes, the staging test with negative and mutation controls, and the new hook across target states, theme switches, a headless install and the upgrade migration step. Other post-theme hooks and desktop commands were stubbed. The full upgrade script, a desktop session and Home Manager activation were not run.
